title: Catch-All Routes
definition: An extension of dynamic routes using an ellipsis `[...param]` that captures an array of nested URL segments, rather than just one.
simpleExplanation: A standard dynamic route `[id]` only catches ONE slash (e.g. `/shop/shirts`). A catch-all route `[...categories]` catches infinite slashes (e.g. `/shop/mens/shirts/summer/red`). It gathers all those words into an array and hands them to you.
realWorldExample: Creating a complex e-commerce filtering system or a documentation site where the URL depth varies wildly (`/docs/react/hooks/useState`).

basic: What syntax is used to create a catch-all route folder?
intermediate: What is the difference between `[...slug]` and `[[...slug]]` (double brackets)?

answers.question: Syntax?
answers.answer: An ellipsis followed by the variable name in square brackets: `[...slug]`.

answers.question: Single vs Double brackets?
answers.answer: `[...slug]` requires at least ONE segment (e.g., `/shop/shirts`). `[[...slug]]` is an OPTIONAL catch-all, meaning it will also match the root route (e.g., just `/shop` with no sub-categories).
